name: Phenome: the big picture
description: A configurable product is defined once. The same definition gives the customer a preview, is frozen into a snapshot that is priced and ordered, and produces the files production works from. The model names protocols and the requirements on them, never a product, tool or technology. Each module is a unit of code of its own; modules exchange only the objects drawn between them, and every such object is a protocol with a contract. How a module meets these requirements is stated by its implementation, not here. Every requirement has an identifier (such as SNP-2); an implementation of the engine is conformant when each identifier is covered by a passing conformance test that names it. Handbook references: modules M01 to M32, boundaries B01 to B24.

author.description: An engineer who writes or prototypes a configurator.

designer.description: A person who builds a configurator in conversation with an AI agent.
designer.note: Open decision D1: who this person is. The answer decides whether drafts may run on shared infrastructure and whether the agent may write code or only a graph.

customer.description: A person who configures and buys a product.

salesPerson.description: A person in the business who checks an imported order and releases it to production.

geometryKernel.description: Computes geometry for a definition. Must give the same result for the same inputs wherever it runs, on the customer's side and on the authoritative side.
geometryKernel.note:
**Requirements.**

- KRN-1: The same inputs give the same result on the customer's side and on the authoritative side.

nurbsBackend.label: NURBS backend
nurbsBackend.description: Computes on NURBS curves, surfaces and solids for the kernel. Takes and returns plain data, so the kernel's own types do not depend on it.
nurbsBackend.note: Open decision D7: whether it is available on the customer's side or on the authoritative side only.

fieldEngine.description: Evaluates signed distance fields and returns meshes and point sets.
fieldEngine.note: Open decision D6: a second engine beside the kernel, or a prototype to retire.

authoringLibraries.description: The model tree and parts model, the operation catalogue, dataflow graphs and sketching: everything a definition is written against.

inspector.description: Builds a definition, runs it and answers its whole state; exports the published UI schema. Its answer to a failed build carries the full diagnostic text.
inspector.note:
**Requirements.**

- INS-1: A failed build is answered with the full diagnostic text.

Handbook boundary B03.

authoringWindow.description: Shows an author the tree, the knobs and the scene of a definition through the inspector. Not tied to any visual editor.

visualEditor.description: A node-based visual programming editor with its own geometry runtime.

canvasLink.description: Provides provider-neutral agent access through MCP to 2D and 3D content applications. Application adapters expose sessions, documents, capabilities and explicit targets, retain application-specific tools and coordinate conflicting writes across clients.

canvasOperations.description: Offers the kernel's operations as components in the visual editor and converts geometry between the editor's types and the kernel's at that edge only.

surfaceAnalysis.description: Measures continuity across the boundaries between surfaces and reports numbers; the judgement stays with the author.

configuratorComponents.description: Lets a canvas declare itself a definition: parameters, node tree, BOM rows, artifacts and displayed values, answered through the same UI-generator protocol as a code definition.

agentKit.description: Everything an AI agent needs to produce a definition: the rules of a definition as a knowledge file in every new project, the inspector's operations as agent tools (new, catalogue, run, set, apply, UI schema), and a context pack for assistants without tools. Must not assume any particular agent.
agentKit.note: An organisation may restrict which agents may see its clients' data; that rule belongs to the organisation, not to the kit.

agentApp.description: A conversation with an AI agent beside a view of the result, for people who do not work with a coding agent.

aiAgent.label: AI agent
aiAgent.description: A language model that writes the definition's code, graph or canvas.

previewGenerator.description: Runs a definition on the customer's side and draws the scene. Its results are never authoritative: nothing priced or ordered rests on them.
previewGenerator.note:
**Requirements.**

- PRV-1: Nothing priced or ordered rests on a preview result.

generatorService.description: The authoritative generator: many sessions, revisions, the freeze, limits on time and memory per run.
generatorService.note: Open decision D4: one service for all clients or one per client.

canvasRunner.description: Runs canvas definitions on the authoritative side.
canvasRunner.note: Needed only if canvas definitions are sold to customers (open decision D5).

customerUi.label: Customer UI
customerUi.description: The configurator a customer sees. Built only from the published UI schema and the scene; embeddable in a web page and in a shop.

shop.description: Product pages, cart and checkout. Owns the payment transaction (handbook M13).
shop.note: Open decision D2: the shop or the ERP owns the catalogue (handbook M03).

pricingModule.description: Prices a valid snapshot. Never computes geometry.
pricingModule.note:
**Requirements.**

- PRM-1: The pricing module never computes geometry.

Handbook M10, M11.

artifactStore.label: Snapshot and artifact store
artifactStore.description: Keeps snapshots and the files they reference, addressed by content hash, and never changes a stored item.
artifactStore.note:
**Requirements.**

- ART-1: A stored item is addressed by content hash and never changed.

Handbook M09.

productionExport.description: Writes the production files of a snapshot from its part tree: the exchange model with the assembly tree and exact solids, the BOM, drawings, cut lists, and the archive with its manifest.
productionExport.note: Meets PRD-1 to PRD-5 of the production files.

erp.label: ERP
erp.description: Owns sale orders and accounting. Imports an order request as a confirmed sale order.

definition.description: A configurator at a version, with its published UI schema.
definition.note:
**Requirements.**

- DEF-1: A definition is verified when the inspector builds it, runs it once without error and exports its UI schema; this check is what compatible with Phenome means, whoever or whatever wrote it.
- DEF-2: A factory reads nothing but its inputs.
- DEF-3: Inputs are plain values: numbers, booleans, strings, enumerations.
- DEF-4: A published definition is never changed, only superseded by a new version.

codeDefinition.description: A definition written as code: one model with its factories and nodes.

canvasDefinition.description: A definition drawn on a canvas and marked up with the configurator components.

uiSchema.label: UI schema
uiSchema.description: The published inputs and displays of a definition, pruned to what is published.
uiSchema.note:
**Requirements.**

- UI-1: Every node and input has an identifier that survives structural change; an index or a position is not an identifier.
- UI-2: The schema carries no human-readable text; labels and translations belong to the UI.
- UI-3: The schema holds only what the definition publishes.

canvas.description: A prototype drawn in the visual editor.

recipe.description: A canvas written out as data: components, wires, typed-in values, sliders with bounds.

continuityReport.description: Continuity measured along each boundary between two surfaces: position, tangent and curvature deviations.

conversation.description: What the person and the AI agent said, with the drafts the agent produced.

configuratorBrief.description: What the configurator must do, in the words of the person who wants it: product and purpose, users, inputs with ranges and defaults, rules, manufacturing limits, price owner and price drivers, production outputs, presentation, host and connected systems, languages, success measures, assumptions.
configuratorBrief.note:
**Requirements.**

- BRF-1: Before writing a definition with a person, the agent interviews them and writes a brief; most people do not know what a good configurator needs, so the agent leads with questions.
- BRF-2: Questions come one at a time, in plain words, with a proposed default; the whole interview for a simple product stays under fifteen minutes.
- BRF-3: Every published input of the definition traces back to an entry of the approved brief; assumptions are listed for the person to confirm.
- BRF-4: Writing the definition starts only after the person approved the brief; later changes go into the brief first.

configuration.description: The values a customer chose, at a session revision.
configuration.note:
**Requirements.**

- CFG-1: A configuration addresses inputs by the UI schema's identifiers.
- CFG-2: Every change raises the revision; a result computed for an older revision never overwrites a newer one.
- CFG-3: Entries whose identifiers no longer resolve are reported, never applied to another input.

Handbook M04, B03.

scene.description: What the view draws: meshes and their placements.
scene.note:
**Requirements.**

- SCN-1: Every placement maps back to the node it came from.
- SCN-2: Nodes with identical inputs to one factory share one mesh.

snapshot.description: One frozen revision: definition and engine versions, inputs, BOM, cost drivers and artifact references.
snapshot.note:
**Requirements.**

- SNP-1: Only the authoritative generator produces a snapshot.
- SNP-2: A snapshot is immutable once written.
- SNP-3: A snapshot carries every version it depends on, so it can be recomputed and checked.
- SNP-4: The same configuration of the same definition version gives the same snapshot hash.

Everything after the configurator depends on it. Handbook B05, B09.

hash.description: A content hash of the snapshot.

productionFiles.description: Files referenced from the snapshot by content hash: cut list, drawings, production data, later machine programs.
productionFiles.note:
**Requirements.**

- PRD-1: Production receives one archive per order, named with the order number and the date, with a manifest listing every file and its content hash.
- PRD-2: The archive contains a STEP model with the assembly tree and exact B-rep solids, one product per part.
- PRD-3: The archive contains a BOM as PDF and as data, and the BOM agrees with the STEP tree.
- PRD-4: The archive contains the configuration it was computed from.
- PRD-5: The same snapshot gives the same archive bytes.

priceResult.description: A price for one snapshot, with its validity and the gaps it could not fill.
priceResult.note:
**Requirements.**

- PRC-1: A price result names the snapshot it priced.
- PRC-2: A price result expires no later than its snapshot.
- PRC-3: The price comes from the owner of prices through the pricing contract, with the time it was computed.

shopOrder.description: An order in the shop with one custom line per configured product.
shopOrder.note:
**Requirements.**

- SHP-1: Each line carries the snapshot reference and the price from the pricing module; the shop sets no price of its own for a configured product.

orderRequest.description: A frozen snapshot with its price, sent to the ERP for import.
orderRequest.note:
**Requirements.**

- ORD-1: The idempotency key of an order request is the channel together with the channel's own order line reference; the same key returns the existing order. The snapshot hash identifies the configuration, not the order: two orders of the same configuration are two orders.
- ORD-2: The same key with a different payload (another snapshot, another quantity or price) is a conflict.
- ORD-3: A channel's order number is kept as an external reference and never becomes the ERP's own identifier.
- ORD-4: The import checks the total against the price owner and refuses a mismatch.

saleOrder.description: The confirmed sale order in the ERP.

topologyOptimisation.description: Distributes material in a design domain under loads and supports so that a goal such as stiffness is best for a given amount of material, and returns the material layout as a density field.
topologyOptimisation.note: Added by the owner on 2026-10-20 as a module of its own, not part of the Field Engine. The first implementation is a GPU prototype; fluid problems (CFD) may join later. Licences of everything it ships must allow publishing.

designDomain.description: The space material may occupy, with its supports, loads, material and the allowed amount of material.

materialLayout.description: The optimised distribution of material in the design domain as a density field, with the value of the goal it reaches.

furniture.description: Parametric furniture parts a definition is assembled from: boards with their material, edge banding, grain and machining, and the assemblies built of them, such as a cabinet carcass, a drawer or a door, each part with inputs of its own and a stable identifier.
furniture.note: Added by the owner on 2026-10-23 as a module of its own (decision P22). It starts from a single board of a kitchen cabinet; the construction rules come from the kitchen and furniture kits written for the interiors portal. Its cut list reaches production through the production export.

authoring.description: Writing a definition as code and checking it.

prototyping.description: Sketching in the visual editor and translating the sketch to code.

emitting.note: The part of the canvas made of catalogue operations translates mechanically; the rest is translated by hand or by an agent.

surfaceChecking.description: Checking the continuity of freeform surfaces on the canvas.

briefing.description: Interviewing the person about the product before anything is built.

agentAuthoring.description: Building a definition with an AI agent through the agent kit.
agentAuthoring.note: The result passes the same verification as hand-written code. Open: the agent writes code or a dataflow graph.

agentAppConversing.description: The same work inside the agent app.

canvasMarkup.description: Turning a canvas into a definition with the configurator components, without translation to code.
canvasMarkup.note: An AI agent can build the canvas too, through the canvas link.

configuring.note: A canvas definition has no preview on the customer's side; every change of a value goes to the authoritative side.

freezing.description: The authoritative run that turns a configuration into a snapshot.

modelRunning.note: The NURBS backend only for NURBS geometry, the field engine only for distance-field geometry, the canvas runner only for canvas definitions.

expiring.note: A snapshot expires with the shortest validity among its dependencies: prices, stock, tariffs.

ordering.description: Ordering from the product's own web page.

checkingOut.description: Ordering and paying in the shop.
checkingOut.note: After payment the shop sends the order request to the ERP.

releasing.description: Checking an imported order and its files and releasing it to production.
releasing.note: Production itself stays outside the model until the handbook's production boundaries (B14 onwards) are worked on.

topologyOptimising.description: Finding where material should be in a part before its geometry is modelled, from the loads and supports the author sets.

writeDefinitionAsCode.title: Write a configurator as code and publish it
writeDefinitionAsCode.story: As an author I want to write a configurator as code and publish it, so that customers can configure the product.

steps.does: Creates a definition from the template and writes the model, its factories and its inputs.
Builds the definition and runs it once. A failed build comes back with the full diagnostic text.
Shows the tree, the knobs and the scene. The author turns knobs and reads the displayed values.
Fixes what the numbers show and repeats until the displayed values are right.
steps.problem: If node identifiers depend on position, a structural change moves saved values onto other nodes.

steps.does: Exports the published UI schema and marks the definition published.

doneWhen: The definition builds, runs once without error and exports a UI schema.
Every published input has an identifier that survives a structural change.

prototypeOnCanvas.title: Prototype on a canvas and translate the sketch to code
prototypeOnCanvas.story: As an author I want to sketch a product on a canvas and get code from the sketch, so that a prototype becomes a definition without retyping it.

steps.does: Sketches the product on the canvas, with sliders for the values a customer will change.
Computes the sketch live while the author works.
Writes the canvas out as a recipe: components, wires, values, slider bounds.
Translates the part of the recipe made of catalogue operations into code.
Translates the rest by hand or with an agent.
steps.problem: A component with no catalogue operation has no translation. Each one is a request for a new kernel operation.

steps.does: Verifies the definition.

doneWhen: Every slider of the sketch is an input of the definition, with the slider's bounds.
The translated definition passes verification.

markUpCanvas.title: Turn a canvas into a configurator without code
markUpCanvas.story: As an author I want to declare a canvas a configurator with components, so that a product drawn in the visual editor can be sold without translating it to code.

steps.does: Draws the product on the canvas.
Declare the canvas's parameters, node tree, BOM rows, artifacts and displayed values.
Runs the canvas with the declared parameters.
Hands the definition over for verification.
Verifies the definition.
steps.problem: Model gap: verification is drawn for code definitions only. A canvas definition needs a verification path of its own.

doneWhen: A channel cannot tell a canvas definition from a code definition by its answers.

buildWithOwnAgent.title: Build a configurator with any AI agent
buildWithOwnAgent.story: As a designer I want to describe a product to the AI agent I already use and get a working configurator, so that I do not have to learn the model's code.

steps.does: Creates a project with the kit and says what product it is for.
Interviews the designer one question at a time: who uses it, what changes between variants, ranges, rules, price owner, production files, where it lives.
steps.problem: Most people have never specified a configurator; without the interview the agent builds what it guesses.

steps.does: Reads the brief, corrects it and approves it.
Gives the agent the rules of a definition, the catalogue of operations and the inspector's tools.
Writes the definition and asks the inspector to build and run it.
Answers the whole state, or the full diagnostic text when the build fails.
Turns knobs through the kit's tools and checks displayed values, child counts and shared meshes.
steps.problem: The agent reads numbers, not the picture. Whether the product looks right is the designer's check.

steps.does: Looks at the result and asks for changes until it is right.
steps.problem: An organisation may forbid some agents for its clients' data. The kit cannot enforce that.

doneWhen: The definition passes the same verification as hand-written code.
Every published input has a unit, bounds and an identifier that survives a structural change.

buildInAgentApp.title: Build a configurator in the agent app
buildInAgentApp.story: As a designer without a coding agent I want to build a configurator in a conversation beside a view of the result, so that I can see the product while it is being built.

steps.does: Describes the product in the app.
Passes the conversation and the kit's tools to the agent.
Supplies the rules, the catalogue and the inspector's tools.
Writes the definition and has it built and run.
Verifies the definition and returns its state.
Shows the result beside the conversation.
steps.problem: Open decision D1: if anyone may use the app, drafts must never run on shared infrastructure without isolation.

doneWhen: A definition built in the app is indistinguishable from one built with a coding agent.

configureProduct.title: Configure a product and see it change
configureProduct.story: As a customer I want to change a product's dimensions and options and see the result at once, so that I can find the variant I need.

steps.does: Opens a session on the published definition.
Changes the width.
Recomputes the product on the customer's side.
Draws the new scene and the displayed values.

doneWhen: A change of a value shows without a round trip for code definitions.
The configuration's revision rises with every change.

getPrice.title: Get a price for a configuration
getPrice.story: As a customer I want a price for exactly what I configured, so that I can decide whether to buy.

steps.does: Asks for a price.
Runs the definition authoritatively for this revision.
Stores the production files under their content hash.
Writes the snapshot.
Prices the snapshot.
steps.problem: A partial price must say which part is missing. A total over missing parts is not a price.

steps.does: Shows the price with its validity.

doneWhen: The price names the snapshot it priced.
The same configuration of the same definition version gives the same snapshot hash.

orderFromProductPage.title: Order from the product's own web page
orderFromProductPage.story: As a customer I want to order the configured product from its page, so that the order carries exactly what I configured.

steps.does: Confirms the order.
steps.problem: This path has no payment. It suits quotes and business customers; who collects payment is not modelled.

steps.does: Shows the confirmation with the price and its validity.
Imports the order request as a confirmed sale order.

doneWhen: The sale order refers to the snapshot hash and carries the production files.

buyInShop.title: Buy a configured product in the shop
buyInShop.story: As a customer I want to put a configured product in the shop's cart and pay, so that I can buy it like any other product.

steps.does: Adds the configured product to the cart.
Creates an order line with the snapshot reference and the price from the pricing module.
steps.problem: The shop must not set its own price for a configured product.

steps.does: Pays.
steps.problem: If the snapshot expired between cart and payment, the order is priced again before payment, not accepted at the old price.

steps.does: Sends the order request to the ERP.
Imports the order request as a confirmed sale order.

doneWhen: The shop's order number is stored in the ERP only as an external reference.

orderCarriesFiles.title: Production files arrive with the order
orderCarriesFiles.story: As a sales person I want every sale order to carry the files production needs, so that nobody re-draws a configured product.

steps.does: Runs the definition and produces the BOM and cost drivers.
Stores the production files under their content hash.
Attaches the files to the imported sale order.
Checks the order and its files and releases it to production.
steps.problem: Production is outside the model so far; what happens after the release is not drawn.

doneWhen: Each file on the order matches the hash recorded in the snapshot.

returnToSavedConfiguration.title: Come back to a saved configuration
returnToSavedConfiguration.story: As a customer I want to open a configuration I saved earlier, so that I can order it later or change it.

steps.does: Opens the saved configuration.
Applies the saved values by identifier and draws the product.
steps.problem: If the definition was superseded, values whose identifiers no longer resolve are shown to the customer. A value is never dropped silently.

steps.does: Asks for a fresh snapshot, because the old one expired.
Freezes the configuration again.
Prices it.

doneWhen: A saved configuration opens on the version it was saved with, or shows exactly what changed.

snapshotExpires.title: An old price is not honoured
snapshotExpires.story: As the business I want a snapshot to expire when its prices or stock may have changed, so that nothing is sold at a price that no longer holds.

steps.does: Marks the snapshot expired when the shortest validity among its dependencies ends.
Refuses to price an expired snapshot.
Asks for a fresh snapshot before showing a price.

doneWhen: No price is shown or charged for an expired snapshot.

duplicateOrderRequest.title: The same order sent twice creates one order
duplicateOrderRequest.story: As the business I want a repeated order request to return the existing order, so that a retry after a timeout never creates a second order.

steps.does: Sends the order request.
Hears nothing back and sends the same request again.
Finds the same channel order line already imported and returns the existing order.

doneWhen: The same channel order line returns the same order.
The same channel order line with a different payload is reported as a conflict.
Two different orders of the same configuration create two orders.

publishNewVersion.title: Publish a new version of a configurator
publishNewVersion.story: As an author I want to publish a new version without breaking saved configurations and placed orders, so that a product can change after it is on sale.

steps.does: Changes the definition.
Verifies and publishes the new version.
Opens new sessions on the new version. Existing snapshots keep the version they were frozen with.
steps.problem: Saved configurations of the old version need a rule: carry values over by identifier, report what could not be carried.

doneWhen: An order placed on the old version is produced from the old version.

configureCanvasProduct.title: Configure a product defined on a canvas
configureCanvasProduct.story: As a customer I want to configure a product whose definition was drawn on a canvas, so that it sells like any other product.

steps.does: Changes a value.
Sends the run to the canvas runner.
Runs the canvas definition.
steps.waits: a server round trip per change
steps.problem: Model gap: the authoritative side yields no scene, so the model has no preview for canvas products. Open decision D5.

steps.does: Shows the result when it arrives.

doneWhen: A canvas product can be priced and ordered through the same snapshot as a code product.
